evidence.source: Development fast-lane rollout run 31012556164 on bc4d00dc; contract 112 applied 5 August 2026. The lane proved the pending set additive by reading the migration before applying it. Corroborated read-only afterwards: the ledger holds 112 rows through 20260805080000. public.provider_entity_map exists and is EMPTY, with row level security enabled, ZERO policies, and zero grants to anon, authenticated, service_role or PUBLIC — so no browser session can reach it. All five new predictor_internal objects are deployed BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed migration: provider_mapping_gaps md5 e0bdc02fe0489ddc398c1d4c5956fb8b over 1651 characters, resolve_provider_round 7eca16f7cc79e8df13f98dc0ffaf7f89 over 244, resolve_provider_season 9a31d0caefa8e2feec3ee9c5ae4960c5 over 191, resolve_provider_team 0c5a7a2794971dcdd5e718cff7dcd364 over 230, and touch_provider_entity_map 1c4318bee4240d4113d86fad7eb15623 over 53. Every one is security definer with search_path pinned to the empty string, and none is granted to any browser or service role. The scoping that matters survived the apply: the team key is FOREIGN KEY (tournament_id, team_id) REFERENCES teams(tournament_id, id) and the round key is the matching composite, so the hosted database itself refuses to map a provider identifier onto a club in a different competition season. Five CHECK constraints, four unique indexes and the one updated_at trigger are present. Behaviour-neutral on development today: the map is empty and has no caller.
